correctness.rationale: PASS: Verified index normalization Y_i=(X_i+X_{i+1})/2, sign(Y_{i+1}-Y_i)=sign(X_{i+2}-X_i). The r prescribed signs split into two independent monotone rankings on parity coordinate chains; either alternating orientation has probability q_r=1/[(floor(r/2)+1)!(ceil(r/2)+1)!], so event probability p_r=2q_r. For overlap displacement d<r, two alternating windows agree only if their shared sign is consistent; their union is a single r+d alternation of probability p_(r+d). For r<=d<=r+1, the windows share at most s<=2 original innovations, and conditioning on them multiplies any complete rank-order probability by at most (m)_s<=m², bounding joint event by m²p_r². Disjoint windows at d>r+1 are independent. The 1989 Arratia--Goldstein--Gordon local-dependence theorem with neighborhoods |d|<=r+1 and b3=0 gives a conservative TV bound of the displayed b1+b2 form. For λ_n=(n-r)p_r bounded and r=o(sqrt n), both (n-r)m²p_r² and (n-r)q_(r+1) decay because q_(r+1)/q_r ~1/r; p_r->0. Union bound and floor((n+1)/(r+2)) disjoint event blocks give finite tail sandwich. With Stirling, r≈(1±epsilon)log n/loglog n gives summable dyadic upper/lower failure bounds; monotonicity fills intermediate n for a.s. scale. Independently enumerated full innovation-rank permutations for r<=5 and verified p_r=1,1/2,1/6,1/18,1/72. No finite test is treated as infinite proof.
